edges: H.G. Wells introduces the character Hallery who is obsessed with the Mind of the Race.
H.G. Wells portrays General Joffre as a representation of the common man and the finest qualities of the Allies' war.
H.G. Wells describes his first encounter with the King of Italy, noting the monarch's lack of pomp.
H.G. Wells expresses confidence that the Allies will ultimately defeat Germany through new tactics.
H.G. Wells describes a tour of a munitions factory given by André Citroën.
H.G. Wells sees a possibility of victory in 1917 but acknowledges the war may continue into 1918 or 1919.
